It never decides whether a problem is catalogued: a blocked problem stays, and its `needs` are what the library builds next.

problems.title: Pathwise uniqueness for the square-root rough-Heston variance equation
problems.statement:
Fix $H\in(0,1/2)$, $v_0>0$, $\nu>0$, and a Brownian motion $W$. Consider nonnegative continuous adapted solutions satisfying $\sup_{t\leq T}\mathbb E[V_t^p]<\infty$ for every finite $T$ and $p\geq1$, of

$$V_t=v_0+\frac{\nu}{\Gamma(H+1/2)}\int_0^t(t-s)^{H-1/2}\sqrt{V_s}\,dW_s.$$

If $V$ and $\widetilde V$ use the same Brownian motion and initial value on the same filtered probability space, must they be indistinguishable on every finite horizon? A proof or a counterexample settles this question. This is already a concrete case of rough Heston, with constant initial forward variance and zero mean reversion.
problems.background: Strong simulation and coupling arguments need control of solutions driven by the same noise, beyond determining their distribution.

lean_statement.note: The library has the Itô integral and Lipschitz SDEs; it lacks the solution notion of a stochastic Volterra equation (#532).

known_results: Weak existence and uniqueness in law are available for this affine Volterra model.
Pathwise uniqueness holds after localizing away from zero; the square-root boundary is the difficulty.
For a singular kernel $(t-s)^{-\alpha}$, Prömel–Scheffels require diffusion Hölder exponent $\xi>1/[2(1-\alpha)]$. With $\alpha=1/2-H>0$, this excludes $\xi=1/2$.

sources.title: Forde–Gerhold–Smith, Small-time VIX smile and the stationary distribution for the Rough Heston model
sources.finding: Explicitly says pathwise uniqueness is unknown even for constant initial variance; distinguishes weak uniqueness and localization.

sources.title: Prömel–Scheffels, Pathwise uniqueness for singular stochastic Volterra equations with Hölder coefficients
sources.finding: The full regularity assumption is stronger than one-half Hölder for singular kernels; Remark 2.2 alone is not the theorem.

problems.title: Physical Stefan uniqueness when jumps accumulate at time zero
problems.statement:
Let $g\geq0$ be a bounded integrable density on $(0,\infty)$ and $B$ a standard Brownian motion. Define

$$X_t^x=x+B_t-\Lambda_t,\qquad \tau^x=\inf\{t\geq0:X_t^x\leq0\},\qquad
\Lambda_t=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P(\tau^x\leq t)g(x)\,dx.$$

Require $\Lambda$ to be nondecreasing and càdlàg and to obey the physical minimal-jump rule. Writing
$\mu_{t-}(A)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P(\tau^x\geq t,\,X_{t-}^x\in A)g(x)\,dx$, this rule is
$\Delta\Lambda_t=\inf\{z>0:\mu_{t-}((0,z])<z\}$, with the corresponding initial rule.

Assume the initial rule gives no jump at zero and a finite global minimal physical solution $\underline\Lambda$ exists. In the remaining regime where $\Delta\underline\Lambda_{t_n}>0$ for some $t_n\downarrow0$, is the physical solution unique? Prove uniqueness in this regime or construct one admissible $g$ with two distinct physical solutions.
problems.background: The loss process models contagious defaults in a mean-field system; uniqueness determines whether the same initial balance-sheet distribution determines a single loss evolution.

lean_statement.note: Needs the physical solutions of the supercooled Stefan problem (#533); Brownian motion and hitting times exist.

known_results: Muñoz reduces global uniqueness to short-time uniqueness and rules out accumulation of jumps at positive times for integrable initial data.
Blore–Hambly Theorem 3.1 gives global uniqueness when the minimal solution is continuous on some (0, epsilon). Remark 3.9 isolates accumulation at zero as the remaining possible mechanism.
Uniqueness of a maximal weak solution in the separate free-target formulation is not, by itself, uniqueness among all physical solutions here.

problems.title: Relaxed equilibrium existence with action-dependent diffusion under time inconsistency
problems.statement:
Consider an infinite-horizon diffusion on $\mathbb R^d$ with compact action set $U$ and relaxed Markov policies $\pi(x,du)$. Its generator is

$$\mathcal L^\pi f(x)=\int_U\left[b(x,u)\cdot\nabla f(x)+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}\big(a(x,u)D^2f(x)\big)\right]\pi(x,du),\qquad a=\sigma\sigma^\top.$$

The current self evaluates a policy by $J^\pi(x)=\mathbb E_x[\int_0^\infty\int_U r(s,X_s,u)\pi(X_s,du)\,ds]$, with non-exponential time dependence. An equilibrium permits no positive first-order gain from a deviation over $[0,\varepsilon]$ followed by the prescribed policy.

Extend the relaxed-equilibrium existence theory of Wang–Yu–Zhang–Zhou to covariance $a(x,u)$ that depends on the action. Retain compact controls, uniform ellipticity, coefficient regularity, reward integrability, and the quantitative hypotheses of their existence theorem in appropriate uniform-in-action form; state every additional restriction. The target is an existence and verification theorem for the controlled-diffusion EHJB system, without assuming its solution exists. Any obstruction should identify precisely which proposed extension fails.
problems.background: Portfolio allocations typically affect both drift and variance. An existence theory confined to drift control leaves out that feature.

lean_statement.note: The question asks for an existence theory with its hypotheses, not one proposition; the needed objects make candidate answers statable (#534).

known_results: Wang–Yu–Zhang–Zhou prove existence through vanishing entropy regularization for drift control and explicitly leave controlled diffusion to future work.
Huang–Yu–Zhang establish a convergent policy iteration for regularized drift-control problems and also explicitly leave controlled diffusion open.
Special solvable models and uniqueness under stronger hypotheses do not establish the requested general existence theorem.

problems.title: Integrable Schrödinger potentials for continuum SPX/VIX calibration
problems.statement:
Work at zero rates with positive SPX levels $X,Y$ at dates separated by $\tau>0$ and a nonnegative VIX level $V$ observed together with $X$. Fix their three marginal laws and a reference law $R$ on $(X,V,Y)$. The feasible laws $Q$ obey those marginals and

$$\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid X,V]=X,\qquad
\mathbb E_Q[-(2/\tau)\log(Y/X)\mid X,V]=V^2.$$

For the entropy problem $\inf_Q H(Q\mid R)$, establish explicit hypotheses for continuous marginals under which a finite minimizer admits integrable dual potentials:

$$\log\frac{dQ_*}{dR}=f(X)+g(V)+h(Y)+\Delta(X,V)(Y-X)+\Gamma(X,V)\big[-(2/\tau)\log(Y/X)-V^2\big].$$

The static terms must be integrable under their respective marginals, with the dynamic terms admissible and integrable as required for the dual portfolio. Identify sufficient assumptions and their limits; finite-entropy feasibility alone is not asserted to suffice. The target concerns continuum marginal constraints, beyond a finite-grid multiplier calculation.
problems.background: These potentials justify the semistatic hedge and the dual calibration algorithm, not merely the existence of a calibrated probability law.

lean_statement.note: The question asks for sufficient hypotheses; the feasible set is the shared object (#535).

known_results: Nutz–Wiesel establish integrable potentials for a two-marginal martingale bridge under their assumptions, while explicitly identifying the additional SPX/VIX constraints as unresolved.
Joint SPX/VIX calibration itself is already achieved in the literature.
Recent global multi-maturity feasibility and memory-selection results address a different question from integrable attainment of this entropy dual.

problems.title: A semistatic FTAP for calibrated equivalent martingale measures with finite entropy
problems.statement:
Let $P$ be a reference probability on $\mathbb R^2$ with canonical prices $(X,Y)$ and let $\nu$ be an integrable prescribed law of $Y$, inferred from a full terminal call-price curve. Define

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}(\nu)=\{Q\sim P: Q_Y=\nu,\ \mathbb E_Q[Y\mid X]=X,\ H(Q\mid P)<\infty\}.$$

Give a necessary-and-sufficient criterion, formulated in terms of semistatic trading opportunities and their appropriate admissibility or closure, for $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}(\nu)\ne\varnothing$. A zero-cost semistatic payoff has the form
$h(X)(Y-X)+g(Y)-\int g\,d\nu$.

The criterion must distinguish equivalent from merely absolutely continuous measures, impose the entire terminal law, and account for finite relative entropy. Simply restating measure existence, or using the usual FTAP for a finite menu of options, does not answer this question.
problems.background: This would characterize when exact option calibration can stay equivalent to a physical model at finite information cost.

lean_statement.note: The question asks for a criterion; a candidate criterion is statable once both objects exist (#535, #536).

known_results: Nutz–Wiesel–Zhao assume nonemptiness of this class in (1.3), then prove the entropy-minimization and semistatic-utility results. They explicitly ask for a trading criterion for that assumption.
Non-closedness of semistatic payoffs is a central obstruction.
Pennanen–Perkkiö provide broad semistatic duality results with a finite set of statically traded derivatives; that does not directly impose a full terminal law.

problems.title: Does the expected signature determine the law of the signature of Brownian motion stopped at a domain exit time?
problems.statement: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded $C^{2,\alpha}$ domain, $B$ a Brownian motion started at $x\in\Omega$, $\tau$ its first exit time from $\Omega$, and $S(B)_{[0,\tau]}$ the (Stratonovich) signature of the stopped path. Is the law of $S(B)_{[0,\tau]}$ determined by its expected signature $\mathbb E[S(B)_{[0,\tau]}]$? (Chevyrev-Lyons guarantee this when the expected signature has infinite radius of convergence; for $2\le d\le 8$ the radius is finite everywhere.)
problems.background: The moment problem for random signatures underlies kernel and two-sample methods and signature-based model identification.
known_results: Chevyrev-Lyons (Ann. Probab. 2016, arXiv 1307.3580): expected signature determines the law if its radius of convergence is infinite.

Boedihardjo-Diehl-Mezzarobba-Ni: finite radius for the unit disc; Li-Ni (arXiv 2011.07917): finite radius everywhere on bounded C^{2,alpha} domains, 2<=d<=8, so the Chevyrev-Lyons sufficient condition fails there.

problems.title: Robust American hedging duality for non-càdlàg payoffs under semimartingale-characteristic uncertainty
problems.statement: Work in Rodrigues' nondominated framework: a family $\mathcal P$ of laws on path space under each of which the canonical price $S$ is a semimartingale whose differential characteristics lie in a prescribed measurable set-valued map, with the universally completed right-continuous filtration $\mathcal G$. For an adapted American payoff $\xi=(\xi_t)_{t\le T}$ of class (D) under every $P\in\mathcal P$, Rodrigues proves, when $\xi$ is càdlàg, that the Snell envelopes $Y^P_t=\operatorname{ess\,sup}_{\tau\ge t}E^P[\xi_\tau\mid\mathcal G_t]$ aggregate into one process and that the superhedging duality $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\sup_\tau E^P[\xi_\tau]=\inf\{x:\ x+\int Z\,dS\ge\xi\ \mathcal P\text{-q.s.}\}$ holds with a minimal hedge. Do the aggregation and the duality with a minimal hedge still hold when $\xi$ is an arbitrary optional process of class (D), not càdlàg? (For the dominated class of all equivalent local martingale measures of one market, irregular payoffs are covered by arXiv 2611.05116; the question is the nondominated, characteristic-uncertainty case.)
problems.background: American-option superhedging under uncertainty is the natural dynamic-stopping extension of robust hedging duality; regularity of the payoff is the remaining technical gap in the semimartingale-characteristics framework.
known_results: Rodrigues (2025): aggregator of Snell envelopes and robust hedging duality for cadlag class-(D) American payoffs in general semimartingale (jumps allowed, non-vanishing diffusion) uncertainty.
Guo-Oblój (2025): continuous-semimartingale prices with adapted closed convex volatility constraints, duality via randomised stopping times and optimal transport.
Chau-Rasonyi (2024, 2411.19206): American superhedging duality with cone constraints and local viability (different uncertainty model).

problems.title: A mimicking Markov martingale for every peacock, Markov for the raw filtration
problems.statement: Let $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ be a weakly continuous peacock on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$ (increasing in convex order). Pammer-Robinson-Schachermayer show that after Gaussian regularisation $\mu_t*\gamma^\eta$ there is a strongly Markov martingale It\^o diffusion with these marginals, and exhibit peacocks (counterexamples, with the Markov property taken w.r.t. the usual-conditions filtration) with no mimicking Markov martingale without regularisation. Open problem as stated by the authors: when the Markov property is defined with respect to the RAW (natural, non-augmented, non-right-continuous) filtration, is there a peacock admitting no mimicking Markov martingale?
problems.background: Multidimensional Kellerer theorem: which marginal families (e.g. calibrated option surfaces on several assets) admit Markovian martingale models.

problems.title: Uniqueness for the Zakai equation of singular-control filtering when control jumps accumulate
problems.statement:
Setting (Calvia-Ferrari): signal $dX_t=b(X_t)dt+\sigma(X_t)dW_t+\,d
u_t$-type process (additively affected by a bounded-variation process $
u$) observed through $Y$; $
u$ is observation-adapted. They derive the Zakai and Kushner-Stratonovich equations and show that the unnormalised filter is the unique density-valued solution of the Zakai equation if $
u$ is continuous or its jump times do not accumulate on $[0,T]$. Open (left by the authors): uniqueness when the jump times of $
u$ accumulate; their suggested route is approximating $
u$ by cutting jumps below $\delta$ and passing to the limit, requiring a tightness property.

problems.title: The optimal local control on the free boundary of the dividend problem for n ≥ 2 insurers
problems.statement: n companies with compound-Poisson surplus processes $X^i$, dividend rate/lump-sum controls with weights, switching (Azcue-Muler multidimensional model, $\delta$-approximation); the optimal value function is a viscosity solution of the HJB system. In dimension one the optimal strategy is a band strategy because the free boundaries are free points where all incoming premium is paid out. Open (stated by the authors): in $n\ge2$, determine the optimal local control on the free boundary between the non-action region and a dividend-payment region (they conjecture dividends paid at a rate keeping the surplus on the boundary, or lump sums), and decide whether a band-type/curve structure is optimal in general.
problems.background: Multi-dimensional dividend control is the benchmark for cooperating insurers.

problems.title: The duality l(L^∞) = E' for the robust multi-period binomial model
problems.statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be a convex set of probability measures on a measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$. Let $E$ be the space of finite signed measures absolutely continuous with respect to at least one $P\in\mathcal P$ (total variation norm), let $L^\infty=L^\infty(\mathcal P)$ be the space of $\mathcal P$-quasi-surely bounded measurable functions modulo $\mathcal P$-q.s. equality, and let $l:L^\infty\to E'$, $l_h(\mu)=\int h\,d\mu$. The map $l$ is an isometric embedding with weak$^*$-dense range, and the question is whether the range is all of $E'$. For $T=1$ and the robust binomial model of Blanchard--Carassus (parameter box $(u,d,\pi)\in E_0$, $\Omega=(0,\infty)$, $S_1=S_0Y_1$), one has $l(L^\infty)=E'$ on a canonical extension of the model (Klein--Köstenberger). Question: for $T>1$, does the robust multi-period binomial model of Blanchard--Carassus (uncertainty set generated by the same parameter box at each of the $T$ steps), or any non-trivial robust multi-period binomial model, satisfy $l(L^\infty)=E'$ (on the model or on its extension)? A proof or a counterexample settles it. The exact uncertainty set is the one fixed in the cited papers.
problems.background: The quantitative Halmos--Savage theorems and the robust FTAP for large financial markets of Cuchiero--Klein--Köstenberger--Schmidt assume l(L^infty)=E'; without it the multi-period extension of their robust asymptotic-arbitrage theory is not available.
known_results: For T=1, l(L^infty)=E' holds for the robust binomial model after a canonical extension (Klein--Köstenberger, arXiv 2605.04912, Section 5.3 and Corollary 46).
l(L^infty) is always weak* dense in E' (Lemma 3.4 of arXiv 2504.06686), so the issue is weak* closedness.

Klein--Köstenberger (Lemma 40, Remark 41) show the supports of the T=1 sub-families are not disjoint in general and that this already occurs for multi-period; the disjoint-support route of the one-period proof therefore does not transfer directly.

problems.title: Complete mixability of the uniform law on a convex body of ℝ^d for n ≥ d + 1
problems.statement: For a convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, is the uniform distribution on $C$ $n$-completely mixable on $\mathbb R^d$ (there exist $X_1,\dots,X_n$ uniform on $C$ with $\sum X_i=n\,\mathbb E X$ a.s.) for every $n\ge d+1$? Wang notes the statement is equivalent to the case $n=d+1$. Known for $d=1$ ($n\ge2$) and, for $d=2$, only the projections are $3$-CM.
problems.background: Sharp upper/lower bounds for VaR/ES of sums of risks with given marginals reduce to mixability and convex-order-minimal dependence.
known_results: d=1: uniform on an interval is n-CM for n>=2 (Gaffke-Ruschendorf 1981).
Projection of an n-CM law to any subspace is n-CM; concave-density laws on R are n-CM for n>=3 (Puccetti-Wang-Wang 2012).

problems.title: Complete mixability of absolutely continuous laws on a bounded interval for all large n
problems.statement: Let $F$ be an absolutely continuous distribution on a bounded interval $[a,b]$. Is there $n_0$ such that $F$ is $n$-completely mixable (centre $n\mu$) for all $n\ge n_0$? Known: this holds if the density $f$ satisfies $f\ge 3/(n(b-a))$ on $[a,b]$ (Puccetti-Wang-Wang 2013), hence for every density bounded away from zero. Open: remove the positive lower bound.
problems.background: Sharp upper/lower bounds for VaR/ES of sums of risks with given marginals reduce to mixability and convex-order-minimal dependence.
known_results: Density bounded below by 3/(n(b-a)) implies n-CM (Puccetti-Wang-Wang 2013).
Necessary mean condition a+(b-a)/n <= mu <= b-(b-a)/n; sufficient for monotone densities (Wang-Wang 2011).

problems.title: When do the sums with given marginals have a smallest element in convex order?
problems.statement: For marginals $F_1,\dots,F_n$ let $D_n=\{X_1+\dots+X_n: X_i\sim F_i\}$ (any joint law). When does $D_n$ contain an element $S_0$ with $S_0\le_{\rm cx}S$ for all $S\in D_n$? Find necessary and sufficient conditions on $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$. Known: not always (Bernard-Jiang-Wang 2014, Example 3.1); exists when all $F_i$ have decreasing densities (Bernard et al. 2014); for Bernoulli classes it always exists (Cossette et al. 2024, as reported by a search summary of arXiv 2309.17346-related work).
problems.background: Sharp upper/lower bounds for VaR/ES of sums of risks with given marginals reduce to mixability and convex-order-minimal dependence.
known_results: Counterexample class exists; smallest element exists for decreasing densities; Bernoulli marginals always have one (cited from search summary, not opened).
